strings: A grim trail begins with Deliah's Ring, found among the Rot Hide gnolls’ corpse piles in Silverpine Forest. Its inscription, “For Deliah,” points back to a plague victim taken from Tirisfal’s mass graves.

Among the gnoll mounds in Silverpine Forest, a ring rests on the pockmarked hand of a relatively fresh corpse. The band bears a simple inscription: “For Deliah.” The Rot Hide gnolls are doing more than scavenging battlefields. They raid the mass graves of Tirisfal Glades and carry human and Forsaken corpses south to Fenris Isle for their own purposes.

High Executor Hadrec sends the ring to Brill, where Magistrate Sevren keeps records of the recently deceased. Sevren confirms that Deliah lived in Brill and died of the plague. She was buried before body-snatchers exhumed her remains. The ring leads to the grief of those she left behind, and to the question of whether mortal devotion can endure undeath.
The ring is found among the Rot Hide gnoll mounds in northern Silverpine Forest, on the hand of an unwrapped plague victim among the scavenged dead.

Keryn Sylvius sends a sealed parcel from Goldshire to Master Mathias Shaw in Stormwind. The delivery gives a promising rogue entry into SI:7's inner workings.

A parcel from the Lion's Pride Inn to the Stormwind Barracks may look like ordinary courier work. For a budding rogue, it is an audition for Stormwind Intelligence. Local trainer Keryn Sylvius entrusts the package to novice cutpurses, giving them a direct introduction to Master Mathias Shaw. The delivery tests whether they can cross the capital quietly, keep a low profile, and follow discreet orders without asking questions.

The handoff brings an operative into SI:7 headquarters in Old Town. Mathias Shaw uses such deliveries to separate pretenders from true talents. Those who present the parcel without faltering receive high-stakes field assignments, beginning with covert reconnaissance and infiltration against Defias smuggling networks in Elwynn Forest.

The parcel stays sealed to its courier. It may hold intelligence reports, trainee assessments, or confidential material about local threats such as the Defias Brotherhood in Elwynn.

Deviate Hides are the mutated skins stripped from the beasts dwelling within the Wailing Caverns. Warped by the corrupting dream of the druid Naralex, these otherworldly pelts are sought by druids looking to repurpose the nightmare's taint into durable leather goods.

When the night elf druid Naralex entered his deep slumber beneath the Barrens, his dream turned into an Emerald Nightmare that warped the local cavern ecology. The beasts lurking in the depths transformed into unnatural deviate predators with tough, mutated hides. While inherently touched by evil, these pelts possess unusual, supple resilience that makes them uniquely suited for leathercrafting. Nalpak, perched high above the cavern mouth in the skull-shaped rock formation, collects these hides to study their properties and fashion them into sturdy utility packs.

Deviate hides come from creatures warped by the Emerald Nightmare seeping out of Naralex's slumber. This corruption alters their flesh, bestowing strange, otherworldly durability and elasticity that ordinary beast pelts lack.

Near Agamand Mills, Devlin Agamand’s bones carry a bitter legacy. The younger son of the wealthy family that owned the mills, he roamed the road by his ruined home as a mindless Scourge thrall. A traveler struck him down and brought his remains to a survivor in Brill, who sought vengeance.

Devlin Agamand lived in the shadow of his elder brother Thurman. Thurman was gentle and tall, while Devlin was frail and sharp-tongued. When the Plague of Undeath swept through northern Tirisfal Glades, the Agamand family failed to protect its lands and laborers. Devlin was among the first to fall. The Scourge raised him as a ravenous ghoul, and his mad chattering haunted the roadside leading to Agamand Mills.

Coleman Farthing lives in Brill and holds a deep grudge against the Agamand bloodline. He blames the family for failing his own when the plague came. Farthing sent travelers to lay Devlin to rest and gather his remains. He wanted Devlin’s bones on his mantle, to savor how his former masters had been reduced to dust and shattered fragments beneath his heel.

Devlin was the younger son of the wealthy Agamand family, who owned Agamand Mills in northern Tirisfal Glades. His mild-tempered, broad-shouldered brother Thurman stood in sharp contrast to Devlin, who was frail, sickly, ill-tempered, and sharp-tongued.

Disarming Colloid is a specialized chemical agent formulated to counter the volatility of Seaforium explosive powder. Provided by the dwarf Ashlan Stonesmirk in the Wetlands, it serves as the crucial stabilizing component in a neutralizing mixture meant to prevent a catastrophic demolition of the Stonewrought Dam.

When Ashlan Stonesmirk analyzed the unusual blasting powder left by Dark Iron sappers at the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan, he recognized it immediately by its distinct scent and fine silver crystals: Seaforium. While harmless when completely dry, Seaforium becomes immensely destructive upon contact with moisture, making it an existential threat to the waterlogged Stonewrought Dam. To halt this reaction before a detonation occurs, Stonesmirk provided a disarming colloid. When combined with three specific local reagents—lurker venom, crushed Mo'grosh crystal, and a crocolisk tear—this colloid effectively neutralizes the explosive properties of the Seaforium compound.

It serves as the base chemical agent needed to defuse Seaforium explosive powder. When mixed with lurker venom, crushed Mo'grosh crystal, and a crocolisk tear, it neutralizes the volatile reaction that would otherwise cause a catastrophic explosion when the Seaforium gets wet.

The Divined Scroll is an enchanted parchment used by the night elves of Silverwind Refuge to unmask the source of Ashenvale's disturbed waters. By channeling the residual magic within intact water elemental bracers, the scroll reveals the identity of the rogue spellcaster summoning them.

The tainted waters of Mystral Lake have long troubled the Sentinels guarding Ashenvale. To pinpoint who is manipulating the water elementals infesting the lake, Sentinel Velene Starstrike provides travelers with an uncharged divining scroll. By gathering intact bracers directly from the slain elementals and using them as an arcane reagent, the latent bindings within the metal bleed into the parchment. The resulting Divined Scroll exposes the magical signature of the rogue wizard behind the infestation.

Once energized, the script upon the Divined Scroll points Sentinel Velene directly to a mortal culprit: a reckless mage deliberately corrupting the pristine woodland pools. Armed with the revelation penned across the parchment, the Sentinels are able to plan retribution and send scouts to hunt down the summoner responsible for despoiling their sacred wilderness.

In recent times, the remaining orcs have begun gathering strength once more under Chieftain Nek'rosh, raising their war banners over encampments northeast of Menethil Harbor.
